A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCER. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching despite revisions and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SCER experiments across six benchmarks, including component ablations, environment-inference experiments, visual analyses, and timing results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional results for extreme correlations, noisy inferred environments, and comparison with GroupDRO-ES.

M1.justification: The group-mean directions, alignment losses, combined objective in Equations 1–3, and training updates remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 explicitly adds domain labels d to its input list, documenting information already used in v1 rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: The six benchmark tasks remain. v2 extends ColorMNIST coverage to 99% spurious correlation and noisier inferred environments, and adds a coarse four-group CivilComments scenario with a broader sample pool. These are extensions within the existing vision and language tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds GroupDRO-ES as an evaluated comparator in Table 16 and includes GroupDRO in the expanded Grad-CAM comparisons. Baselines omitted from the shortened main tables remain in appendix Tables 11–13 and 15, so those omissions are not comparator removals.

E3.justification: New Table 16 uses a separately cited experimental configuration, including a four-group CivilComments split with 269,038 training examples. Table 14 tests approximately 70% accurate environment partitions while retaining other Table 4 settings. The original main experimental budgets, metrics, and splits remain; newly explained annotation and checkpoint-selection practices are disclosures.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends robustness and representation analyses: it adds the 99% correlation stress test, tests degraded environment inference, introduces Waterbirds t-SNE comparisons, and replaces the single Grad-CAM example with comparisons including GroupDRO and additional cases. Existing loss-weight sensitivity, norm ablation, correlation plots, and timing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with seeds 0, 1, and 2 and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. However, v2's new Table 16 reports only point estimates for MultiNLI and four-group CivilComments, introducing a limited inconsistency in uncertainty reporting. No increase in runs or new statistical test is stated.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores are retained, including the full comparisons relocated to the appendix. Substantial new results include SCER's 56.0 ± 2.2 worst-group accuracy at 99% correlation and EIIL+SCER's 65.1 ± 2.8 average accuracy with noisy partitions. Table 16 adds four GroupDRO-ES comparisons under different settings; these are new results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the core-term coefficient in Theorem 1 from 1 to 1/2, revises Proposition 1's class-mean signs, and rewrites the subgroup-error derivation. The ± sign now identifies the worst subgroup rather than an alleged classifier-sign equivalence. v1's multiclass/multidomain Proposition 2, Theorem 2, and associated derivations are removed.

C1.justification: The introduction changes factors that 'guarantee' worst-group error to factors that 'influence' it, while the abstract presents the theory as motivation. This narrows the theoretical framing alongside removal of the formal multiclass extension. The central embedding-regularization and superior worst-group-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale for Gaussian embeddings with shared covariance and explicitly acknowledges the strength of the extreme-correlation assumption. It also interprets the new noisy-environment and visualization results as evidence of robustness beyond accurate group inference and of representation differences from GroupDRO.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly explains training/validation annotation availability and worst-group checkpoint selection, supported by Table 10. It also documents the four-group CivilComments construction and sample counts. Algorithm 1 clarifies the domain-label input; the existing hyperparameter search spaces and code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Seddik et al., Papyan et al., and Lai and Muthukumar to support its theoretical assumptions, and Selvaraju et al. for Grad-CAM. It gives greater attention to early-stopped GroupDRO as a competitive comparator. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the prose, expands explanatory passages and the conclusion, and reorganizes baseline discussion around abbreviated main comparisons and complete appendix results. The main section sequence remains recognizable. Conference-status text, an affiliation, and acknowledgments are also updated.

P2.justification: Main Tables 1, 2, 3, and 5 are condensed, with complete comparisons displayed in appendix Tables 11–13 and 15. v2 adds annotation-availability and experimental tables, a t-SNE figure, and expanded Grad-CAM displays. The original correlation plot is retained as Figure 4. Conference formatting, captions, and page layouts are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects important coefficient, sign, and subgroup-error mistakes in the central binary derivation and strengthens empirical validation through GroupDRO-ES comparisons and targeted robustness tests. Annotation and model-selection disclosures also improve assessability. Removing the multiclass proof narrows formal coverage, and uncertainty reporting is incomplete in part of Table 16, but the central theoretical repairs and stronger validation provide a substantial net improvement.
